section_summary.extract_value: This section details the testing of Hypothesis 2, which examined the interaction between participants' goal orientations (learning, prove, avoidance) and training conditions on performance. Moderated regression analyses revealed no significant effects for learning goal orientation. However, significant interaction effects were found for prove goal orientation (explaining 6% and 4% additional variance for first and second test phase performance) and avoidance goal orientation (5% added explained variance for second phase performance). The results indicated that high prove and avoidance goal orientations were beneficial in the error avoidant training condition.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details moderated regression analyses investigating the interaction effects of participants' goal orientations (learning, prove, avoidance) and training conditions on performance across two test phases. The study found significant interaction effects for prove goal orientation (on both first and second phase performance) and avoidance goal orientation (on second phase performance), but no significant effect for learning goal orientation, providing partial support for Hypothesis 2. Table 3 presents the hierarchical regression results.
